newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-O'Reilly sees no offer for UK paper.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-O'Reilly sees no offer for UK paper.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Plc chairman Tony O'Reilly on Friday dismissed as groundless speculation that he aimed to double his company's stake in Britain's Independent daily by buying out partner Mirror Group Newspapers Plc.
"That's an absolute fiction," O'Reilly said in a telephone interview.
International media group Indepedent Newspapers of Dublin owns 46 percent of the Independent, as does the Mirror Group Newspapers Plc.

The Mirror Group earlier denied an article in the Guardian newspaper that O'Reilly, also chairman of U.S. food group H.J. Heinz, had offered 60 million stg for Mirror's holding in Independent Newspapers Plc.

O'Reilly said the ownership structure was an editorial and business advantage since the Independent would be the sole leading British newspaper free of party or ideological allegiances as Britain elects a new national government in 1997.
"A paper that is not speaking for a proprietor or an ideology is going to be very important as a tie-breaker in the election," O'Reilly said.
